items.basis: 2026 has 261 Mon–Fri days. Statutory holidays (Mt. 102 §) on weekdays: 1 Jan (Thu), 3 Apr Good Friday, 6 Apr Easter Monday, 1 May (Fri), 25 May Whit Monday, 20 Aug (Thu), 23 Oct (Fri), 25 Dec (Fri) = 8 (15 Mar, Easter Sunday 5 Apr, Whit Sunday 24 May, 1 Nov fall on Sunday; 26 Dec on Saturday). Official swaps: rest days Fri 2 Jan, Fri 21 Aug, Thu 24 Dec, worked Saturdays 10 Jan, 8 Aug, 12 Dec — net zero for a Mon–Fri plant (3 days off, 3 Saturdays worked). 261 − 8 − 3 + 3 = 253 days × 24 h = 6,072 h.
items.kind: statute / ministerial decree (as reported by press); weekday arithmetic my own
items.notes: Weekday count and holiday weekdays computed from the calendar (Easter 2026 = 5 April). Without the Saturday swaps (plant does not work the swapped Saturdays) 250 × 24 = 6,000 h. Current book uses 4,000 h a year (UK basis, machines-list.txt) — 34% fewer hours than a 3 × 8 Mon–Fri Hungarian plant runs.

items.unit: years (TAX life implied by the 14.5% straight-line rate)
items.basis: Act LXXXI of 1996 (Tao. tv.), Annex 2 chapter IV: machines and equipment at 33%, 20%, 10% or 7% where specifically listed, and 14.5% for machinery not listed under any of the enumerated items; 100 / 14.5 = 6.9 years. 33% → 3.0 years applies only to the enumerated items.
items.date: rule in force (date of the Q&A pages not shown)
items.kind: statute (as summarised by a tax portal)
items.notes: Whether metal-cutting machine tools appear on the 33% list was NOT confirmed — I take general production machinery as the 14.5% default. Annex 1 point 9 allows 50% first-year depreciation on previously unused assets in the 33% and 14.5% classes (per the same portal). Accounting (Act C of 2000) practice life for machinery: NOT found.
